discrepancies.packet_text: S3's effective edits are mostly unclassifiable by this taxonomy (56-84% OTHER_UNKNOWN per mechanism)
discrepancies.correct_value: Per-mechanism OTHER_UNKNOWN shares in S3_REWRITE are 84.5% (op0), 40.4% (op1), 39.0% (op2), 100% (op3), 100% (op4) — exactly derivable because S3 has only two families (q2: OTHER_UNKNOWN n=3610, CONTROL_COUNT n=2904). The true per-mechanism range is 39-100%, not 56-84%. The 56% endpoint appears to be the POOLED large-displacement OTHER_UNKNOWN share (q3 = 0.5570), not a per-mechanism value; ops 3 and 4 sit at 100% (above the claimed range) and ops 1-2 at ~39-40% (below it, majority CONTROL_COUNT).

discrepancies.packet_text: substitution and copy are the count-changing mechanisms
discrepancies.correct_value: Bitflip burst (op 0) is also a count-changing mechanism in the artifact: in S3, op0 transitions are 15.5% CONTROL_COUNT; in S1, op0's top family is OPERAND_ONLY at only 32.0%, so count-changing families (IO_COUNT/CONTROL_COUNT/combined) account for at least ~36% of op0 transitions. The enumeration as written implies only ops 1 (cell substitution) and 2 (block copy) change instruction-class counts.
discrepancies.source: results/human_taxonomy_redteam.json q1_operator_family_concentration (S1 op0, S3 op0) + classifiers/human_taxonomy_redteam.py family() / substrates/vm_substrates.py mutate() op_index 0

discrepancies.packet_text: The human-taxonomy red team independently notes OP1 is the mechanism whose edits most often change I/O-instruction counts (30% of its effective transitions). (Section 7, S2 DISCLOSURE 2)
discrepancies.correct_value: The artifact records only each mechanism's MODAL family: IO_COUNT is OP1's top family at 29.9%. It does not establish the cross-mechanism superlative: OP2's modal family on S2 is CONTROL_COUNT+IO_COUNT at 37.1%, which also changes I/O-instruction counts, so OP2's I/O-count-changing share is at least 37% > OP1's documented 30%; full per-mechanism family distributions are not committed. Supported claim: OP1 is the only mechanism whose modal edit family is pure IO_COUNT (30%).
